title: Reformed grant historic faith a Spirit gift and intellect perfection
source_text: XLIV. Ex alia vero parte, ut etiam ex antedictis liquere potest, Reformati non negant, & ultro Scholae Romanae Doctoribus concedunt, illam etiam fidem quam historicam vocant, & per quam mens ita praebet assensum Dei Verbo, ut tamen inde voluntas non moveatur ad bene agendum, inter Dei dona debere recenseri, & esse quandam humani intellectus perfectionem, per quam hominum mentes illuminantur in cognitione veritatis illius quae per se salutaris est: & illos qui sunt ista fide donati in maxima culpa esse quod ad propriam salutem tali lumine non utantur, quod scilicet, ex se & sua natura justitiae & salutis viam hominibus ostendit.
pass_a_gloss: On the other side, as also can be clear from what was said before, the Reformed do not deny, and freely concede to the Doctors of the Roman school, that that faith too which they call historic, and by which the mind so gives assent to God Word that yet the will is not moved thereby to doing well, ought to be counted among God gifts, and is a certain perfection of the human intellect by which people minds are illuminated in the knowledge of that truth which is in itself saving: and that those gifted with that faith are in the greatest fault because they do not use such light for their own salvation, since of itself and by its nature it shows people the way of justice and salvation.
pass_b_english: Reformed freely grant Rome that historic faith — assent to the Word that does not yet move the will to well-doing — is among God gifts and an intellect perfection lighting saving truth.
Those so gifted are greatly culpable for not using that light for their own salvation, since by nature it shows the way of justice and salvation.

lemmas.gloss: the faith which they call historic
a perfection of the human intellect

choices.why: Gifted assent without saving use; not mere human history-belief.
